title: WPMS/1811/2015 of Prasant Dobhal AND ANOTHER Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
WPMS No. 1811 of 2015
Hon'ble Manoj K. Tiwari, J.
Mr. Jitendra Chaudhary, learned counsel
for the petitioners.
Mr. S.R. Joshi, learned Standing Counsel
for the State of Uttarakhand.
Petitioners are existing operators, who are
plying their city buses within the municipal
limits of Dehradun. They have challenged the
decision taken by Regional Transport Authority
in its meeting held on 20.05.2015, especially the
one decision taken on supplementary agenda
item No. 1, where the Regional Transport
Authority has held that Vikram Tempo (three
wheelers), Tata Magic and Mahindra Maximo can
also be considered for grant of Stage Carriage
Permit provided these vehicles are suitably
modified for the purpose. This decision taken by
the Regional Transport Authority has been
challenged by the petitioners mainly on the
ground that it is contrary to the provisions
contained in Uttarakhand Motor Vehicles Rules,
2011.
It is the contention of the petitioners that
Vikram Tempo (three wheelers), Tata Magic and
Mahindra Maximo have maximum seating
capacity of six passengers (excluding driver),
therefore, these vehicles cannot be granted Stage
Carriage Permit in view of the provisions
contained in Uttarakhand Motor Vehicles Rules,
2011.
Learned Standing Counsel appearing for
the respondents submits that petitioner, who are
existing operators in respect of different routes,
have no locus standi to challenge the decision
taken by Regional Transport Authority. He
further submits that the decision has been taken
in public interest in view of the provisions
contained in Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 which is a
Central Act and has overriding effect. He further
submits that even otherwise also, the writ
petition is premature, as no stage carriage
permit has been issued to the aforesaid three
categories of vehicles.
Learned counsel for the petitioner also
admits that the stage carriage permit has not
been issued to the aforesaid three categories of
vehicles, thus, this Court finds substance in the
contention raised by learned counsel for the
State that writ petition is premature.

2
In such view of the matter, this Court
declines to interfere with the matter at this
stage. However, this Court hopes and expects
that the Regional Transport Authority will take
any decision in accordance with the Statutory
provision.
With the aforesaid observation, writ
petition is disposed of.
 (Manoj K. Tiwari, J.)
20.02.2020
Aswal
